verses.text: In the second year that Jehoash son of Jehoahaz was king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash began to rule as king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother was Jehoaddin, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, but not as his ancestor David had done. He did everything his father Joash had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.
As soon as he had firm control of the kingdom, he executed the officials who had murdered his father the king.

But he did not put the murderers' children to death. He obeyed what is written in the book of the Law of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Parents must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their parents. Each person must die for his own sin."
Amaziah killed ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He captured the town of Sela in battle and renamed it Joktheel, the name it still has today.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel, with this challenge: "Come, let's meet face to face in battle."

But Jehoash king of Israel sent this answer to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' Then a wild animal in Lebanon came by and trampled the thistle.
You have truly defeated Edom, and now you are proud. Enjoy your fame, but stay at home! Why ask for trouble that will bring you down, and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went to attack. He and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other in battle at Beth Shemesh in Judah.
Israel defeated Judah, and every man of Judah ran home to his tent.

Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash and grandson of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh. Then he went to Jerusalem and tore down its wall from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, a section about one hundred and eighty metres long.
He took all the gold and silver and all the objects found in the LORD's temple and in the treasuries of the palace. He also took hostages, and then he went back to Samaria.
The rest of what Jehoash did, his power, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam became king after him.
Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
The rest of what Amaziah did is written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Some people in Jerusalem made a plot against him, so he ran away to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.
They brought his body back on horses, and he was buried with his ancestors in Jerusalem, in the city of David.
Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
Azariah rebuilt the town of Elath and won it back for Judah, after his father the king had died.
In the fifteenth year that Amaziah son of Joash was king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for forty-one years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.

He won back Israel's borders from Lebo Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south. This was just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had said through his servant the prophet Jonah son of Amittai, from Gath Hepher.
The LORD had seen how bitterly everyone in Israel was suffering, slave or free. There was no one to help Israel.
The LORD had not said he would wipe out the name of Israel from the earth. So he saved them through Jeroboam son of Jehoash.

The rest of what Jeroboam did, all his deeds, his power, his wars, and how he won back Damascus and Hamath for Israel, which had once belonged to Judah, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Jeroboam died and was buried with the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah became king after him.
